deep.reconstruction:
The page is an exercise in sweeping an arrangement of 7 pseudo-lines labelled A..G. It amounts to encoding the arrangement as a sequence of permutations in which each step reverses one or more disjoint adjacent pairs, i.e. a wiring diagram or 'allowable sequence' in the sense of Goodman–Pollack.

The sequence, read from the image (underlined pairs are the ones swapped at the next step):
- 0: ABCDEFG
- 1': ABCEDGF (DE and FG swapped simultaneously)
- 2': ABCEDGF, with DG marked for the next swap
- 3': ABCEGDF (DG swapped)
- 4': ABCGEDF (EG swapped)
- 5': ABGCEDF (CG swapped)
- 6': AGBCEDF (BG swapped)
- 7': AGCBEDF (BC swapped)
- 8': AGCEBDF (BE swapped)
- 9': AGECDBF (CE and BD swapped)
- last line: GAEDCFB (AG, CD and BF swapped)

Every transition is a product of disjoint adjacent transpositions, so the sequence is consistent.

The left-hand column records the crossings: DE and FG, then G crossing successively D, E, C, B, A. Its arrows form a merging tree (DE and FG meet, giving DG, then EG, ...). This tracks the pseudo-line G travelling leftward across the others. At the end, AG is circled as the 'frozen' leftmost pair.

The right-hand drawing shows the same configuration as an arrangement with dashed horizontal sweep lines numbered 5'–11, each passing through the vertex or vertices crossed at that step. These are the sweep levels.

The lower drawings are:
- a small binary merging tree;
- triangular-grid line arrangements (lines in three directions);
- a version with dashed horizontal lines through the vertices, i.e. a sweep of a lattice-like arrangement by horizontal pseudo-lines through the crossing points.

The top-right sketch (a line with a marked point and other lines crossing) is likely about adding a pseudo-line through a given point, in the spirit of Levi's enlargement lemma. This fits the previous page's dashed red/green deformed pseudo-lines through vertices.

The next page completes the picture: the arrangement is drawn in a disk with vertices numbered 1–19, and two wiring diagrams cover steps 1–12 and 12–19. Thirteen of the 21 crossings appear on this page. Purpose: understanding the combinatorial encoding of pseudo-line arrangements by sweeps, as the sequence of transpositions of the order in which the lines meet a moving pseudo-line.
errors: No mathematical errors detected. Every listed permutation follows from the preceding one by disjoint adjacent transpositions.
The final line GAEDCFB is not the full reversal GFEDCBA; the sweep on this page is partial, only 13 of the 21 crossings, and is continued on page 145.

ideas.what: Encoding a pseudo-line arrangement by a sweep: a sequence of permutations of the line labels, each obtained by reversing disjoint adjacent pairs at the crossings met.
ideas.modern_name: Wiring diagram / allowable sequence of permutations (reduced decomposition of the longest permutation, for a simple arrangement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman & Pollack (1980s, allowable sequences); wiring diagrams already in Goodman 1980; reduced words counted by Stanley 1984

ideas.what: Sweeping the arrangement with horizontal (pseudo-)lines through vertices, numbered levels; sweeping lattice-like triangular-grid arrangements.
Adding or deforming a pseudo-line so that it passes through prescribed vertices or points (top-right sketch, continuing page 143).

deep.surprise_reason: Routine working-out of a wiring diagram / allowable sequence for 7 pseudo-lines and sweep pictures. The only historical interest is that Grothendieck was independently handling these standard tools in 1983–84. Nothing appears beyond the known Goodman–Pollack / Edelsbrunner–Guibas framework.
transcription_corrections: The left column of crossings should read DE, FG, then DG, EG, CG, BG, AG; the transcription's 'EG, EG, BG, AG' is misread.
Line 1' is ABCEDGF (the crossed-out attempts are ABCDEFG and AABC...), with DE and FG swapped simultaneously.
Line 2' is ABCEDGF with DG underlined, not a new permutation; 3' is ABCEGDF; 4' is ABCGEDF; 5' is ABGCEDF.
Lines 7'–9' have AG circled; the underlined pairs are CB (7'), EB (8'), and EC and DB (9').
The numbers 5'–11 at the right margin label the horizontal sweep levels of the right-hand arrangement diagram.
